Piano Keyboard 🎹 — dweet d/35177 by dee-gomma
blurb: Someone built a whole animated piano in 140 characters of code, and there's a remix button right there — which means you're about six minutes away from a new side quest.

title: The Mood Board #046 — Brianna Schubert
blurb: It's one creative person's actual monthly brain-dump — Virgo-season resolutions, the fits she wore in Berlin, jobs, odd little finds — and you'll walk away with three new side quests you didn't ask for.

title: Spicy Passion Fruit Mocktail (AKA "Mockarita")
blurb: Four ingredients, but you get to char a jalapeño over open flame for smoky depth — a tiny bit of theatre for a drink that's tart, tropical, and named like it's in on the joke.

title: Tour a Family of Four's Maximalist East Harlem Apartment
blurb: Four people, one apartment, zero fear of colour or clutter — this is the warm, object-stuffed, every-wall-has-a-story energy you keep chasing, and it proves a home can be maximal without ever feeling messy.

title: Cafe Yasuragi, Millenia Walk
blurb: Tucked inside Millenia Walk with deep teal walls and tan leather booths, it's a moody little hideout that basically begs you to bring the film camera and shoot a whole persona in the corner booth.

title: Coffee Receipt Stories
blurb: Tiny illustrated stories drawn on the backs of real coffee receipts by Odding — pure analog, hand-made scrapbook charm, exactly the kind of quiet find you'd want to click through one receipt at a time.

title: WindowSwap
blurb: It drops you into a stranger's window somewhere in the world — ten minutes of someone's laundry line in Tellaro or rain on a Seoul balcony — and it's quiet, weirdly moving, and endlessly re-openable, plus it was built by a couple right there in Singapore.

title: Charlotte Rohde's new typeface has heart-dotted i's and a plan to overwrite problematic men
blurb: A typeface designed as a full character — heart-dotted i's, a feminist bit committed all the way to the end, and a launch campaign shot to look like a photocopier running out of toner — which is exactly the kind of type-as-persona nonsense you'd stay up all night making yourself.

title: Tour a Family of Four's Maximalist East Harlem Apartment
blurb: This is a rental absolutely crammed with color and collected junk-with-soul, and it'll give you permission to stop leaving empty walls and just hang the thing.

title: Cookboys, I12 Katong
blurb: It's a whole 1970s Hainanese cookboy universe built out in vintage signboards and old shopfronts — basically a persona shoot you can order kopi in, and I need you to photograph the signage before anyone else does.

title: Max Bittker's Projects
blurb: This is the whole toybox of the guy who made river.maxbittker.com — falling-sand worlds, generative gardens, tiny strange tools — and I think you'll fall down it for an hour and come out with three new side quests.

title: Poolsuite FM
blurb: It's an entire sun-bleached 90s computer desktop that plays endless summer radio — the kind of committed-to-the-bit web world you'll want to steal interface ideas from while it scores your next side quest.

title: Naive Weekly
blurb: It's a weekly letter from the quiet corners of the internet — hand-made sites, net art, digital gardens — basically the reading version of every web toy you've ever fallen down a hole with.

title: Calamansi Sparkling Margarita Mocktail
blurb: A margarita rerouted through calamansi — that auntie-kitchen citrus you already know by heart — salted rim and all, and endlessly riffable with a chilli-salt rim or a float of pandan syrup.

title: Earthy, Layered Interiors in a Notting Hill Apartment
blurb: This one's a masterclass in making a room feel warm through texture alone — clay tones, worn textiles, soft pools of lamplight — and I think it'd be a dream reference for that lived-in corner you keep almost building.

title: Yunma Bakehouse, Purvis Street
blurb: A brand-new bakehouse hiding behind construction scaffolding off Purvis Street slinging $2.20 pastries — go now, shoot it on film, and feel smug that you found it before the hoarding comes down.

title: Internet Artifacts
blurb: It's a scrollable museum of the early internet where you can actually poke the floppy disks and ICQ pings — pure Y2K-nostalgia raw material for your next persona shoot.

title: Web Curios
blurb: It's one guy, every week, dragging back armfuls of the weirdest and most wonderful things on the internet with running commentary that's funnier than it has any right to be — pure side-quest fuel for you.

title: Doctor Pepo's Tonic (Zero-Proof)
blurb: This one's got apothecary energy — a little spice, a little bitterness, a name fully committed to the bit — and it's exactly the kind of drink worth building a whole evening persona around.

title: Freunde von Freunden — Home Visits
blurb: It's the nosy-friend archive of creatives' actual apartments — unstyled shelves, thrifted lamps, projects mid-sprawl — and it'll convince you that a room full of your own side-quest evidence beats any showroom.

title: MOZmoji 陌迹, Chinatown
blurb: You climb a staircase off Temple Street into a shophouse ceramics gallery where you get to pick your own handmade cup — each one modelled after a season or festival in the Chinese calendar — and then just sit there with cotton cheesecake and black sesame coffee like you live there.

title: Every Place at Once
blurb: It's the Every Noise map rebuilt as cities instead of genres — click Singapore and find out which places on earth are listening like you are, then fall down a rabbit hole into someone else's hometown radio.

title: Dirt
blurb: It's the culture newsletter that treats a Ghibli frame, a dead website and a pop star's tour merch with equal seriousness — exactly your brain, but in essay form.

title: Chrysanthemum Osmanthus Citrus Sparkler
blurb: It's your grandma's dried-flower tea jar turned into a golden, fizzy spritz — heritage flavors you already know by heart, dressed up enough to photograph.

title: A Clinton Hill Brownstone with Chinese Inflections by Bespoke Only
blurb: It's 19th-century Shanghai smuggled into a Brooklyn brownstone — proof you can build heritage into a room as texture and mood instead of hanging it on the wall like a souvenir.

title: Inner Teahouse, Chinatown
blurb: A second-floor shophouse teahouse born out of a pottery studio, where the cups are as considered as the tea — exactly the kind of quiet, hand-made hideout you'd claim as your own and accidentally leave with a new side quest.

title: laurel.world — Laurel Schwulst's site
blurb: It's less a portfolio than a soft cream-colored room you wander through, where every project links sideways to another by year, medium, or friend — the kind of hand-made web object that'll make you want to rebuild your own site by midnight.

title: ★ july newsletter ★ — film friends
blurb: It's a scrappy little film-photography newsletter that reads like a group chat of people who all shoot on expired stock and actually finish their rolls — grainy, warm, and exactly the kind of thing that'll have you digging out the point-and-shoot by Saturday.

title: Lychee Mocktail With Rose
blurb: Canned lychee syrup, rosewater and lime in a glass — it's basically a childhood dessert-stall memory turned into a drink, and that shameless pink is going to photograph beautifully on film.

title: The Modern House — Journal
blurb: Every home in here treats a lifetime of accumulated stuff as the actual decor — books on the floor, one perfect lamp, zero styling — which is permission to let all your side-quest objects live out in the open instead of in bins.

title: Dona Manis Heritage Bakehouse, Katong
blurb: The 30-year-old basement banana pie legend finally got a sit-down room in Katong — and it doubles as a stop on a city-wide Monopoly heritage trail, so your pastry run comes with a built-in side quest.

title: ssh.place — Timelapses
blurb: Watch a whole day of strangers quietly fighting and collaborating over one 200×60 pixel canvas replay as a GIF — it's a tiny communal folk-art archive made entirely in a terminal, and I think you'll want to go claim a corner of it.

title: The radical reasons why you dream of making things by hand
blurb: This one makes the case that your hand-sewn costumes and ancestry archives aren't hobbies but a quiet rebellion — a whole essay arguing that the urge to master something with your hands is the most radical thing you can do.

title: Classic Vietnamese Plum Soda (Soda Xí Muội)
blurb: Salty-sour preserved plum drowned in fizz over cracked ice — it's the nostalgic, slightly feral cousin of every polite floral mocktail, and you get to eat the plum at the end like a prize.

title: Barcelona Remodel by Conti Cert: '70s Style Redux
blurb: You already know how to commit to a persona, so here's a whole apartment doing it — '70s Barcelona reworked with real warmth instead of costume-y nostalgia, and about five ideas in here you could steal for one corner of your place this weekend.

title: Slow Boat Vinyl Listening Café, Tanjong Pagar
blurb: A sibling-run listening café up a shophouse staircase where you pay by the hour and DJ your own afternoon — analogue, unhurried, and made for you and a disposable camera.

title: WigglyPaint
blurb: Every line you draw squirms and squeaks like it's alive, and you can export the whole wobbly mess as a GIF — it's the most charmingly imperfect drawing tool on the internet and I fully expect to see it in your next persona shoot's title cards.

title: Tedium: The Dull Side of the Internet
blurb: It goes absurdly deep on the unglamorous stuff — dead software, forgotten gadgets, weird old fonts — and every issue reads like a side quest someone left out for you to pick up.

title: Pandan Colada (Mocktail)
blurb: It's kaya toast and pandan chiffon cake reincarnated as a creamy green tiki drink — zero proof, absurdly photogenic, and exactly the kind of thing you'd make a whole persona shoot around.

title: The Selby — Inside Creative People's Homes
blurb: It's basically permission to let your rooms look like your brain — every shelf, taped photo and inherited lamp doing the decorating for you.

title: Labyrinth — Asia's 50 Best 2026, No. 40
blurb: It's your whole heritage-meets-remix obsession plated up — chai tao kuay and chilli crab reimagined by a chef who refuses to serve anything that didn't grow here, and exactly the kind of place worth inventing an occasion for.
